descriptive_contrast.assumptions: The ACS replicate weights represent the sampling and weighting variability; the descriptive target makes no counterfactual claim
descriptive_contrast.estimand: How much more the uninsured share fell in the cohort states than in the comparison states, as a finite-population descriptive contrast (no causal claim)
descriptive_contrast.estimator: Same regression and same coefficient as the policy ledger
descriptive_contrast.randomness: ACS sampling of addresses (households) within strata; nothing about which states expanded is treated as random
descriptive_contrast.target_population: civilian and military household population ages 19–64 with family income at or below 138% of the poverty threshold (IPUMS POVERTY 1–138), in the 30 design states, 2011–2019, with the states and their policies taken as given
descriptive_contrast.title: The same number as a survey description of fixed states
descriptive_contrast.variance_estimator: Successive difference replication with the 80 ACS person replicate weights, scale 4/80, df 79; CRV1 by household as an approximation

policy_inference.assumptions: Parallel trends between cohort and comparison (assumed, not established); no anticipation; no spillovers across states; states' shocks independent of one another; the stated cohort and exclusion rules
policy_inference.estimand: Average effect of the 2014 expansion on the uninsured share among people in the expansion cohort, 2014–2019 (an ATT), under parallel trends
policy_inference.estimator: PERWT-weighted linear probability model with state and year fixed effects; equivalently WLS on state-year means weighted by population
policy_inference.explicit_weights: PERWT (ACS person weight) to represent each state-year population; cells enter stage two in proportion to their weighted population
policy_inference.implicit_weights: Regression weights across states and years: each state's contribution depends on its population and on its within-state variation in treatment; larger states count more
policy_inference.randomness: Assignment of expansion across states (the policy was chosen state by state), plus ACS sampling of households within each state-year
policy_inference.target_population: civilian and military household population ages 19–64 with family income at or below 138% of the poverty threshold (IPUMS POVERTY 1–138), in the 30 design states (January 2014 expansion cohort and states not expanded by 2019), 2011–2019
policy_inference.title: Medicaid expansion and uninsurance: inference for the policy comparison
policy_inference.variance_estimator: CRV1 clustered by state with t(29); CRV3 jackknife and wild cluster restricted bootstrap as few-cluster checks; randomization inference over assignment as a sensitivity
